content_pages.basis: model reading; differs from the triage proposal on [16]

evidence: content pages read off the renders

variety.method: Composition per page is the extractor's archetype (composition.archetypes): the page's content boxes (layout and master chrome and recurring furniture left out, the title kept) leader-clustered by slide_similarity, the Hungarian assignment of box IoU over the larger set, at 0.5. Exhibit structure per page is read from the file (ooxml.exhibit_facts): native charts by their plot types and series counts, tables, pictures, drawn shapes, panels; nobody names it. Content pages are library.py's triage proposal (cover, divider, disclaimer, hidden and generated pages are not content) until /variety/content_pages answers it.
weaknesses: Boxes only: a full-width table and a full-width bullet block of the same extent are one archetype; what the boxes hold is not compared.

Arrangement, not kind: a table beside a chart, mirrored or re-weighted, is a different arrangement to box IoU (such pairs score 0.30 to 0.40), so the realised composition cannot see that kind of sameness; the exhibit structure read from the file, and the plan's named compositions, are where it shows.

Leader clustering is order-dependent and not transitive: a page joins the first archetype whose anchor it matches, so two pages that match each other but not an earlier anchor can land in different archetypes.
The title is content to the extractor, so pages that differ only below the title look more alike than the build's frame-free measure sees them: the reference is held to the more lenient count.
On a PDF the reader's text blocks stand in for shapes, and a page set as many small blocks rarely matches another at 0.5, so a PDF reference can read every page as its own archetype.
V counts adjacent pairs only: an arrangement used on every other page (A B A C A) reads 1.0; distinct compositions per page is the figure that shows it.

A picture carries no structure: a reference that pastes its charts and tables as pictures reads every such page as 'picture', so its structure V is low and the build is held to a lenient line; what the picture shows is the digest's reading, never measured.

A PDF states rectangles, paths and text, never a chart or a table, so a PDF reference's structure reads only pictures, drawn shapes and text, coarser than a native build's: the two are held to each other as change rates, each over its own pages.
Structure is kind and count, not form: two column charts of three series are one structure whatever they compare, and a waterfall drawn as stacked columns is a stacked column chart.
